title: The Sweet Postcard
premise: Ezra Voss, a struggling novelist, arrives in the coastal town of Marrow Bay to research his next book and discovers that his rival author, Paloma Oyelaran, has written a bestselling novel based on the one reckless week they shared in their twenties — a week he fled without explanation. A snowstorm traps them together in her grandfather's lighthouse, forcing old wounds, buried truths, and unfinished love to surface. As the town's midwinter festival approaches, Ezra must choose between protecting his pride and confessing the secret that made him run: he abandoned a manuscript, and a promise, that could have changed both their lives. He risks his whole heart at last, and they end the festival together, co-writing the sequel neither could finish alone.
about_author: Ivo Brightwater is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent a decade writing letters for sailors before turning to fiction. Known for storm-swept romances set on northern coasts, Ivo writes from a cottage that leans, like its owner, toward the sea.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse on the Dust Jacket
chapters.summary: Ezra Voss's POV. Ezra arrives in Marrow Bay to research a novel and recognizes the lighthouse on a bookstore display — it belongs to Paloma Oyelaran, his rival, whose new bestseller is unmistakably about their shared past. Shock and dread set the emotional beat: the past has been published without his permission.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma spots Ezra at the town café and realizes he's read her book; her bravado masks guilt over using their history without asking. Flashbacks reveal their week in their twenties — and his disappearance. The beat is defiant vulnerability: she wrote the truth because he never gave her one.

chapters.title: Snowbound at the Light
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. A sudden snowstorm traps Ezra at the lighthouse when he comes to confront her; the roads close, the generator fails, and Paloma grudgingly offers the guest room. Forced proximity sparks old banter and sharper wounds. The beat is reluctant intimacy crackling under resentment.

chapters.title: Chapters We Never Wrote
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped together, they read each other's old manuscripts and argue over who betrayed whom — her with the book, him with the vanishing. Paloma reveals she waited a year before giving up. The beat is raw excavation: the truth begins costing more than the lies.

chapters.title: What the Storm Buried
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. Ezra nearly confesses why he left — the failed manuscript and the promise he made her dying grandfather — but a phone call from his agent about a film deal for Paloma's novel interrupts, and he learns the deal hinges on 'the real story.' The beat is cowardice resurfacing at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Festival of Small Lights
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The storm lifts; the town prepares its midwinter festival, and Paloma's grandmother pressures her to honor the late grandfather by lighting the old beacon. Paloma asks Ezra to stay through the festival, testing whether he'll run again. The beat is cautious hope extended like an open hand.

chapters.title: Rival Lines
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. Ezra's agent pushes him to publicly claim his share of 'the real story,' threatening to expose Paloma's source and humiliate her. Torn between loyalty and ambition, he drafts a betrayal instead of a confession. The beat is the price of survival pressing on the scales against love.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma discovers Ezra's abandoned manuscript hidden in the lighthouse — written for her, ending mid-sentence the night he left. She confronts him before the festival crowd, demanding the truth he's withheld for a decade. The beat is shattering exposure: the whole heart, finally demanded.

chapters.title: Lighting the Beacon
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. At the festival's climax, Ezra publicly declines the deal, confesses his secret — the promise to her grandfather, the shame of failure — and asks for a second chance he doesn't believe he's earned. Paloma must choose before the beacon is lit. The beat is the leap: risking everything with no guarantee.

chapters.title: The Sweet Postcard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Paloma lights the beacon and answers with the postcard Ezra sent her twenty years ago — the one word he never explained, now finally understood as 'stay.' They begin co-writing the sequel in the lighthouse kitchen. The beat is warm resolution: timing was never the obstacle; courage was.
